score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 7 major vendors (EmailListUS, Principals-EmailList, K12Data, SchoolDataLists, EducationDataLists, BookYourData, HighSchoolPrincipalMarketing) currently selling school superintendent and principal databases ranging from 17K to 5M+ education contacts with 98% email deliverability claims and commercial pricing models. Six high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) education technology (EdTech) vendors (Google for Education, Clever, Canvas LMS, PowerSchool SIS, Schoology, ClassLink, Seesaw) selling learning management systems, student information systems, single sign-on platforms, classroom collaboration tools, and assessment platforms at $5-$25 per student per year — with average district enrollment of 3,800 students, a single district contract generates $19,000-$95,000/year in recurring revenue, making EdTech vendors willing to pay $10,000-$25,000/year for targeted superintendent and principal marketing lists; (2) educational publishers and curriculum providers (Pearson, McGraw-Hill, Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, Savvas Learning, Amplify) selling textbooks, digital courseware, supplemental materials, and adaptive learning platforms with district contracts ranging $50,000-$500,000/year depending on enrollment and subject coverage; (3) school safety and security system vendors (Raptor Technologies, Avigilon, Verkada, CrisisGo, Navigate360) selling visitor management systems, surveillance cameras, emergency notification platforms, and threat assessment tools to districts spending $20,000-$200,000 on safety infrastructure; (4) school facilities and operations vendors (HVAC contractors, commercial furniture suppliers like Virco and KI, cafeteria equipment, playground equipment, school bus fleet management, energy management systems) targeting district facility directors and purchasing departments with contracts ranging $100,000-$5M for major capital projects; (5) professional development and teacher training providers (ASCD, Solution Tree, Teaching Strategies, NIET, New Teacher Center) selling in-service training, leadership coaching, instructional improvement programs, and accredited continuing education for teachers and administrators at $10,000-$100,000 per district annually; and (6) school fundraising platforms and parent engagement tools (ParentSquare, Remind, ClassDojo, Konstella, Memberhub) selling communication apps, volunteer coordination, PTA/PTO fundraising platforms, and school event management at $1-$5 per student per year. NCES Common Core of Data (CCD) is the Department of Education's comprehensive public database of all public elementary and secondary schools and school districts, accessible at nces.ed.gov/ccd with district locator tools providing superintendent name, district contact info, enrollment, and operational data. State education departments also maintain public school directories with principal names and school contact information. Zero PII — all professional public education contact data under FERPA exemptions for school officials and public directory information. Engineering lift is low-to-moderate: NCES CCD provides bulk data downloads and searchable district locator; state education department websites provide principal-level data (50 state scrapes or downloads); normalization and deduplication required. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions or custom lists, leaving a clear gap for a one-time $99-$149 CSV. Audience size is substantial: 13,500+ public school districts and 130,000+ public schools nationwide, creating a TAM of 10,000+ potential B2B buyers across EdTech, educational publishing, school safety, facilities, professional development, and parent engagement verticals. Score is 8 due to validated strong willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors with 98% deliverability claims, confirmed authoritative public data via NCES CCD and state education departments, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, large educator population (13.5K districts + 130K schools), and six distinct B2B buyer segments with proven high-value purchasing behavior in the $50B+ K-12 education technology and services market.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all public school district superintendents and school principals extracted from the NCES Common Core of Data (CCD) and state education department public directories — fully public and accessible without authentication. Each record includes the school district or school name, superintendent or principal full name, title, school/district address (street, city, state, ZIP), phone number, website, district NCES ID, school NCES ID, total enrollment, grade levels served (elementary, middle, high), urbanicity (city, suburb, town, rural), locale code, county, and operational status. As of 2026, approximately 13,500 public school districts employ superintendents, and 130,000+ public schools employ principals nationwide. EdTech vendors (Google for Education, Clever, Canvas, PowerSchool, Schoology) pay $10,000-$25,000/year for superintendent and principal marketing lists to sell learning management systems, student information systems, and classroom tools generating $19,000-$95,000/year per district contract. Educational publishers (Pearson, McGraw-Hill, Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, Savvas) targeting district curriculum directors and principals with textbook and digital courseware contracts worth $50,000-$500,000/year. School safety vendors (Raptor, Avigilon, CrisisGo) selling visitor management, surveillance, and emergency notification systems at $20,000-$200,000 per district. Facilities and operations vendors (HVAC, furniture, playground equipment, school bus fleet) targeting district purchasing departments with capital project contracts of $100,000-$5M. Professional development providers (ASCD, Solution Tree) selling teacher training and leadership coaching at $10,000-$100,000 per district annually. Parent engagement and fundraising platforms (ParentSquare, Remind, ClassDojo) selling communication and PTA/PTO tools at $1-$5 per student per year. A one-time $99-$149 CSV undercuts annual subscription vendors while targeting the same B2B buyer segments across the $50B+ K-12 market.

data_wanted: The NCES Common Core of Data (CCD) at nces.ed.gov/ccd is the Department of Education's authoritative public database of all public elementary and secondary schools and school districts. The CCD District Locator (nces.ed.gov/ccd/districtsearch) provides superintendent name, district contact information, phone number, enrollment, and urbanicity for all 13,500+ public school districts. State education departments (all 50 states plus DC) maintain public school directories with principal names, school contact information, and operational data. No authentication required for access. Key fields per district record: school district name, superintendent full name, superintendent title (District Superintendent, Superintendent of Schools, etc.), district mailing address (street, city, state, ZIP), district phone number, district website URL, NCES district ID (7-digit unique identifier), total district enrollment, number of schools in district, urbanicity classification (city, suburb, town, rural), locale code (detailed 12-category classification), county name, operational status (open, closed, reopened). Key fields per school record: school name, principal full name, principal title (Principal, Head of School, Director), school mailing address (street, city, state, ZIP), school phone number, school website URL, NCES school ID (12-digit unique identifier), school type (regular, special education, vocational, alternative), grade levels served (PK, K-5, 6-8, 9-12, etc.), total school enrollment, urbanicity, locale code, county, operational status. Target all active districts and schools (exclude closed/inactive). Scope to district superintendents and school principals only — exclude assistant superintendents, assistant principals, and other administrators (available separately if desired). Approximately 13,500 district superintendent records and 130,000 school principal records nationwide as of 2026. Target output: 143,500 rows combined (13.5K superintendents + 130K principals), or separate files if preferred. Data is 100% public per FERPA exemptions for school officials acting in official capacity and public directory information under 34 CFR § 99.31 and 34 CFR § 99.37.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Six distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior and high contract value justification. (1) EdTech vendors: SIS/LMS platforms generate $5-$25 per student per year ($19K-$95K per district with 3,800 avg enrollment) in recurring revenue; vendors routinely pay $10,000-$25,000/year for superintendent/principal marketing lists (confirmed by K12Data 98% deliverability premium positioning), making a $149 one-time CSV deliver 67×-167× cost savings. A single district contract yields 127×-637× ROI vs. database cost. (2) Educational publishers: district-wide textbook and curriculum adoptions generate $50,000-$500,000/year in sales; publishers pay premium rates for direct access to decision-makers, making a $149 CSV negligible against a single adoption. (3) School safety vendors: districts allocate $20,000-$200,000 on security infrastructure; a single sold system yields 134×-1,342× ROI vs. $149 database. (4) Facilities vendors: capital project contracts of $100,000-$5M for HVAC, furniture, playground equipment make a $149 prospect database trivial — one signed project yields 671×-33,557× ROI. (5) Professional development providers: $10,000-$100,000 annual district contracts for teacher training make a $149 database negligible. (6) Parent engagement platforms: $1-$5 per student per year ($3,800-$19,000 per district) in SaaS revenue makes customer acquisition via $149 database highly ROI-positive. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $1,000 (all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions or custom extracts, not one-time CSV downloads) combined with 98% deliverability claims by premium vendors (K12Data) creates a strong low-price entry wedge. NCES CCD is the authoritative federal source, ensuring data quality and completeness commercial vendors must match.
